speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Your wife mentioned you've been acting agitated and bizarre; can you tell me what has been going on with you lately?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old male. The patient has been demonstrating bizarre and agitated behavior for the past 6 weeks. He believes that he is being spied on by the NSA which is also controlling his mind. His wife adds that he has been increasingly withdrawn and intermittently depressed over the last 3 months. He was terminated from his job 4 weeks ago after he ceased attending work. Since his unemployment, he has been focused on creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: You mentioned believing the NSA is controlling your mind; have you been hearing voices that aren't there, or seeing things others don't? Also, how has your sleep and appetite been over these past few weeks?

speaker: Patient
text: creating a device to prevent people from controlling his mind.

speaker: Doctor
text: I see you are focused on building this device to protect yourself. To help me understand if this is related to a medical condition or substance use, have you used any drugs or alcohol recently, and do you have any family history of psychosis or bipolar disorder?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant medical or psychiatric history reported. Social history: Previously employed. No history of substance abuse reported. Married.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for clarifying that there is no history of substance abuse or significant past medical issues. Given the duration of your symptoms and the nature of your delusions, I need to rule out any underlying organic causes; REQUEST TEST: Urine Drug Screen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The drug screen is negative, which helps rule out substance-induced psychosis. To further assess for organic causes, REQUEST TEST: CT Head with contrast.

speaker: Doctor
text: The CT head is normal, which effectively rules out structural brain lesions or tumors as the cause of your symptoms. Given the 6-week duration of your psychotic symptoms, including delusions of control and paranoid ideas, along with social withdrawal and functional decline, the clinical picture strongly suggests a primary psychotic disorder. DIAGNOSIS READY: Schizophreniform Disorder
